bib.title: BERT Rediscovers the Classical NLP Pipeline
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 57th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (ACL), pages 4593-4601

question: Where in the layers of BERT is linguistic information for each step of the traditional NLP pipeline captured?
hypothesis: inferred: tasks of the traditional pipeline are encoded in the same order as the classical hierarchy (syntax in lower layers, semantics in higher layers).
contributions: An analysis spanning the common components of a traditional NLP pipeline, showing the order in which abstractions are encoded reflects the traditional hierarchy of these tasks.
A qualitative layer-by-layer analysis of individual sentences, showing the model can defer ambiguous decisions or revise incorrect ones using higher-level information.

method.summary: Edge probing classifiers are trained on frozen BERT-base and BERT-large encoders for eight labeling tasks. Layers are pooled with ELMo-style scalar mixing; two metrics (mixing-weight center of gravity and cumulative-scoring expected layer) localise each task in depth. Per-example traces of cumulative probes show out-of-order resolution.
method.task: probing of pre-trained encoder layers with edge probing (POS, constituents, dependencies, entities, SRL, coreference, SPR, relation classification)

datasets.name: OntoNotes 5.0 (POS, constituents, entities, SRL, coreference)
datasets.split: train for probes; dev set for reported F1 and per-example analysis
datasets.preprocessing: Edge probing format via jiant code

other.pretraining: masked language modeling and next-sentence prediction over a 3.3B word English corpus

models.name: ELMo
models.architecture: two LSTM layers over a per-word character CNN

other.used_in: Appendix A.1 only, scalar mixing weights

training.objective: supervised label prediction by a probing classifier per task over frozen encoder activations, with scalar mixing weights learned jointly

other.probe_architecture: architecture and procedure of Tenney et al. (2019), not restated in this paper
other.cumulative_probes: a series of classifiers P(0)..P(L), P(l) mixes layer l and all previous layers; P(0) uses only non-contextual word(piece) embeddings

other.per_example_filter: target edges whose highest-scoring label has average score over layers <= 0.7; sentences with more than one such edge

metrics.name: micro-averaged F1
metrics.definition: common metric across the eight probing tasks

metrics.name: mixing weight center of gravity
metrics.definition: E_s[l] = sum_l l * s_tau(l), the average layer attended to under softmax mixing weights

metrics.name: expected layer (cumulative scoring)
metrics.definition: E_delta[l] = sum_{l>=1} l * delta(l) / sum_{l>=1} delta(l), where delta(l) = Score(P(l)) - Score(P(l-1))

metrics.name: K(*) = KL(*||Uniform)
metrics.definition: non-uniformity of mixing weights s or differential scores delta; higher means lower entropy

baselines: P(0) non-contextual bag of word(piece) embeddings probe
eval.protocol: Main results on 24-layer BERT-large, replicated on BERT-base in the appendix. Single-run dev-set scores; no seeds or significance tests stated.

availability.code: jiant (https://github.com/jsalt18-sentence-repl/jiant) used for the edge probing tasks
availability.data: public benchmark datasets listed above (OntoNotes is LDC licensed)

evidence.quote: trained with a multi-task objective (masked language modeling and next-sentence prediction) over a 3.3B word English corpus

results.claim: Tasks are encoded in a natural progression in depth: POS first, then constituents, dependencies, semantic roles, coreference.
results.setup: BERT-large, edge probing, both mixing weights and cumulative scoring
results.quote: POS tags processed earliest, followed by constituents, dependencies, semantic roles, and coreference

results.claim: Differential (cumulative-scoring) gains are highest in the first few layers for many tasks.
Learned mixing weights are concentrated much later than the differential gains.
Most POS tags are already correct from non-contextual embeddings, so many examples are uninteresting.
results.setup: OntoNotes dev set, BERT-base per-example analysis, layer 0 probe
results.quote: 89% of part-of-speech tags are correct at layer 0

results.claim: Syntactic information is more localizable (concentrated on few layers) while semantic information (relations, SPR) is spread across the network and entity labeling is resolved early with a long tail.
results.setup: BERT-large; high K(s), K(delta) for syntactic tasks, near-uniform mixing weights for relations and SPR

results.claim: The same ordering appears on BERT-base, with task representations concentrating at the same layers relative to the top of the model (stretching effect).
results.setup: 12-layer BERT-base versus 24-layer BERT-large, Figures A.2, A.3

results.claim: On individual examples the model resolves decisions out of pipeline order, e.g. revising entity type from GPE to ORG after resolving the semantic role of Toronto.
results.setup: Qualitative traces, BERT-base, selected OntoNotes dev sentences
results.quote: for individual examples the model is free to and often does choose a different order

results.claim: For ELMo the first LSTM layer is most informative for all tasks and coreference shows only weak concentration.
results.setup: ELMo scalar mixing weights, Figure A.1
results.quote: the first LSTM layer (layer 1) is most informative for all tasks

limits: Exploratory: one encoder family (BERT, plus ELMo mixing weights in the appendix); authors say further work is needed to see if trends hold in general.
Inspection-based probing: a pattern not observed by the probe is not proven absent, and an observed pattern does not show how it is used; behavioural studies are needed.
Cannot say whether weak localization of semantic tasks is BERT difficulty or inherent difficulty of localizing semantics.
Last 1-2 layers can show a drop because new layers may provide distracting features and the probe overfits.
Expected layer is a pseudo-expectation, since F1 is not an expectation over examples.
Probe hyperparameters, dataset sizes and absolute F1 values appear only in figures (not text); per-example analysis uses a heuristic selection of ambiguous sentences and is qualitative.

terms.definition: decomposes structured-prediction tasks into a common format where a probing classifier receives spans s1 and optionally s2 and must predict a label, seeing only per-token contextual vectors within the target spans
ELMo-style softmax-weighted sum over encoder layers learned jointly with the probe; higher weights are read as evidence the layer holds more task-relevant information
series of probes that each see layer l and all earlier layers; differential score is the F1 gain from adding layer l

figures.caption: Summary statistics on BERT-large. Columns on left show F1 dev-set scores for the baseline and full-model probes. Dark (blue) are the mixing weight center of gravity; light (purple) are the expected layer from the cumulative scores.
figures.why: Shows per-task baseline and full F1 and where each task sits in depth, giving the pipeline ordering at a glance.

figures.caption: Layer-wise metrics on BERT-large. Solid (blue) are mixing weights; outlined (purple) are differential scores, normalized for each task. Horizontal axis is encoder layer.
figures.why: Shows localization versus spread per task across layers.

figures.caption: Probing classifier predictions across layers of BERT-base. Blue is the correct label; orange is the incorrect label with highest average score over layers.
figures.why: Shows the model revising a decision (Toronto GPE to ORG) as layers deepen.

code.snippet: h_{i,tau} = gamma_tau * sum_{l=0..L} s_tau^(l) h_i^(l), s_tau = softmax(a_tau)
delta^(l) = Score(P^(l)) - Score(P^(l-1)); E_delta[l] = sum_{l=1..L} l*delta^(l) / sum_{l=1..L} delta^(l)
